summary: Google's Gemma 4 model card and technical report (arXiv 2607.02770, Table 5) report static benchmarks for Gemma 4 31B in thinking mode on bf16 weights; original 5-shot MMLU and GSM8K are not reported. The QAT model cards (google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized, google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-q4_0-gguf) state that QAT preserves quality similar to bf16. None of the published setups matches this harness (zero-shot, non-thinking, greedy, answer-prefilled MMLU), so use these figures as an order-of-magnitude sanity check rather than a pass/fail threshold; the frameworks are judged against each other on identical items.

notes: Google's Table 5 reports all Gemma 4 31B numbers with thinking mode enabled on bf16 weights; this harness evaluates with thinking disabled (`enable_thinking=False`) for deterministic zero-shot comparison across CPU runtimes.

Original 5-shot MMLU is not in the Gemma 4 31B model card; MMLU-Pro (10 choices, reasoning-heavy) is 85.2% with thinking on, so zero-shot 4-choice MMLU on non-thinking 31B should comfortably exceed 75% on healthy checkpoints.

Unlike E2B and E4B, Gemma 4 31B has no Per-Layer Embeddings (`hidden_size_per_layer_input = 0`) and uses uniform 4-bit quantization (`dynamic_wi4_afp32` in LiteRT-LM, `Q4_0` in GGUF, `int4-ov` in OpenVINO) rather than mixed 2-bit/4-bit mobile QAT.
